subject: Meteorology
title: Altimeter Settings
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Altimeter Settings.

hook.text: An aircraft's altimeter measures pressure to determine altitude—but pressure changes constantly with weather.

buildup.text: Pilots set the local altimeter setting (QNH) to correct for current pressure—ensuring accurate altitude readings.

discovery.text: If a pilot flies from high pressure to low pressure without resetting, the altimeter reads too high—dangerously so.

twist.text: The phrase 'high to low, look out below' reminds pilots they're lower than the altimeter shows in falling pressure.

climax.text: Above a set altitude, all aircraft switch to 29.92 inHg—called a standard setting—so everyone uses the same reference.

punchline.text: Same sky, same pressure reference—or you might hit a mountain.

quiz.question: What happens if you fly from high to low pressure without resetting the altimeter?
